answer: Each identity anchors to one listed lighthouse keeper post: a named beacon with a resident keeper, a nightly lamp log under one key, checked each epoch. One post, one identity; a second claim fails, an empty lamp voids it. A fake costs 9,000 units plus 365 sable nights on watch, logged at a walnut desk. Cheapest cheat: hire a stand-in for 6,000 units a year, but they must live at the light and sign under the seller's key, so the seller surrenders their post, one failed live check voids both, and two years cost 12,000 units, more than honest 9,000. 100 fakes cost 900,000 units and 36,500 days.
